title: Clinician Assessment of Laryngeal Disease with Auditory AI before Laryngoscopy: A Paired Reader Study
abstract: arXiv:2611.20050v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Background: Before laryngoscopy, clinicians assess the likely cause of hoarseness and whether to suspect a precancerous or malignant lesion. Whether voice-based artificial intelligence (AI) supports pre-laryngoscopic categorization is unknown.   Methods: We developed an auditory large language model that generates a patient-level assessment card (provisional category, voice-quality ratings, and rationale) and a prespecified malignancy alert from voice recordings, patient information, and acoustic measures obtained before laryngoscopy at one center. We evaluated both in a held-out test set and a later cohort. In a sequential reader study, 32 otolaryngology clinicians categorized held-out cases without AI and, 1 to 2 weeks later, reviewed their initial categories with the card (without the alert). translated_abstract: 背景：在喉镜检查前，临床医生需要评估声音嘶哑的可能原因，以及是否怀疑存在癌前病变或恶性病变。基于声音的人工智能（AI）能否支持喉镜检查前的分类尚不清楚。方法：我们开发了一个听觉大语言模型，该模型基于喉镜检查前在一个中心采集的声音录音、患者信息和声学测量指标，生成患者层面的评估卡（初步分类、嗓音质量评分和依据）以及预设的恶性病变警报。我们在留出测试集和后续队列中对两者进行了评估。在一项序列阅片者研究中，32名耳鼻喉科临床医生首先在不使用AI的情况下对留出病例进行分类，1至2周后，他们结合评估卡（不含警报）重新审视其最初的分类结果。结果：在800次配对评估中，阅片者的准确率在审视前为49.8%，审视后为56.8%（差异为7.0个百分点；95% CI为
tldr: 研究开发的听觉大语言模型评估卡可将耳鼻喉科医生在喉镜检查前判断喉部疾病的准确率从49.8%提升至56.8%。
en_tdlr: An auditory large language model assessment card improved otolaryngologists' pre-laryngoscopic accuracy in categorizing laryngeal disease from 49.8% to 56.8%.
